channel.title: The Leo Chronicle
channel.description: Stories of service, leadership, and impact from the Leo Club of Moratuwa.

item.title: Leo Ape Dansala – July: Sharing Sweetness, Spreading Smiles
item.description: The club commenced this year's Leo Ape Dansala series with a heartfelt ice cream dansala, marking the start of a tradition that will continue every Poya Day.

item.title: Be the Light for Someone
item.description: The world doesn't always need grand gestures to become a better place. Sometimes, all it takes is one person choosing to be a little kinder than yesterday.

item.title: You Are Growing
item.description: A poem on patience, quiet seasons, and trusting that even when nothing seems to be happening, you are still becoming.

item.title: The Quiet Power of Listening
item.description: True leadership is not measured by how loudly we speak, but by how deeply we listen. A reflection on presence, patience, and the strength found in silence.

item.title: Listen to Everyone... But Think for Yourself
item.description: Listening doesn't mean obeying. Not every opinion is truth, and not every piece of advice is right for your life.

item.title: July General Meeting: Strengthening Bonds, Sharing Visions
item.description: Chief Guest Leo Lion Chamal Pramod and district guests joined the club's July meeting to share leadership insights and discuss upcoming projects.

item.title: We Only Have One Earth
item.description: The Earth has always been there for us, asking for nothing in return. Somewhere along the way, we began taking these gifts for granted.

item.title: The Artist by the Lake
item.description: "I don't paint what I see," the old artist said. "I paint what I feel." A short story about seeing beauty in every colour, not only the brightest ones.

item.title: Where Art Meets the Soul
item.description: There is something magical about finding yourself alone with nature. Perhaps that is why art feels so peaceful.

item.title: It's Okay Not to Be Okay
item.description: We often ask each other, "How are you?" and almost without thinking, we reply, "I'm fine." Sometimes those two words hide a heart carrying more than anyone can see.

item.title: Leo Voyage: The Beginning of Every Leo Journey
item.description: A hybrid orientation held with the Leo Club of Prince of Wales College, bringing together 39 aspiring and active Leos to explore the spirit of Leoism.

item.title: Saviya – Session 1: Empowering Dreams Through Entrepreneurship
item.description: 29 participants from unemployed and low-income families learned product costing, pricing, marketing, and business development at Hewagama Junior School.

item.title: Trust & Loyalty: The Bonds That Hold Hearts Together
item.description: There comes a moment in almost everyone's life when the crowd disappears. In that quiet silence, you begin to discover who truly belongs in your life.

item.title: TRI LIFE – Phase 01: Paws of Hope
item.description: Six dedicated Leos travelled around Rawathawaththa, Moratuwa, feeding stray dogs as the first phase of the Paws of Hope initiative.

item.title: What Does It Mean to Be a Leo?
item.description: Being a Leo is about much more than wearing a badge or attending meetings. It's about choosing to make a difference — through leadership, experience, and opportunity.

item.title: ALOKA'26 — Seeking Blessings for a New Leoistic Year
item.description: To mark the dawn of a new Leoistic year, the Leo Club of Moratuwa organised "Aloka '26," an Ashirwada Pooja at Bellanwila Rajamaha Viharaya.
